bib.title: Llama Guard: LLM-based Input-Output Safeguard for Human-AI Conversations

question: Can an instruction-tuned LLM serve as an adaptable input-output safeguard that separately classifies user prompts and model responses against a configurable taxonomy?
hypothesis: Fine-tuning an LLM with the guidelines as input gives a classifier that performs well on its own taxonomy and adapts to other taxonomies by zero-shot, few-shot prompting or further fine-tuning.
contributions: A safety risk taxonomy for interacting with AI agents.
Llama Guard, an LLM-based input-output safeguard fine-tuned on data labeled by the taxonomy, with the taxonomy as input.
Separate instructions for classifying prompts vs responses in a single model.
Public release of the model weights.

method.summary: Llama2-7b is instruction-tuned to output safe/unsafe plus violated category codes given a Llama Guard prompt containing guidelines, classification type (prompt or response), conversation and output format. Trained on 13,997 red-team-annotated prompt/response pairs built from Anthropic harmlessness prompts, with category-dropping augmentation; evaluated by AUPRC in-domain and on ToxicChat and OpenAI Mod by prompting and fine-tuning.
method.task: safety classification of LLM prompts and responses (binary and per-category)

datasets.name: Internal annotated dataset (Anthropic harmless first-turn prompts + Llama-generated responses)
datasets.source: Anthropic human preference data about harmlessness (Ganguli et al., 2022); responses from an internal Llama checkpoint; labeled by in-house red team
datasets.preprocessing: First human prompt kept, assistant response and other turns discarded; badly formatted examples discarded; 4 labels: prompt-category, response-category, prompt-label, response-label

datasets.name: ToxicChat
datasets.preprocessing: binary toxicity label by strict majority vote (>=3 annotators); also used for fine-tuning at 10%, 20%, 50%, 100% of its training data

models.name: Llama Guard
models.context: inferred: 4096 tokens from training sequence length

other.use: fine-tuned on ToxicChat in same setup as comparison

training.objective: language modeling objective on instruction + target (safe/unsafe and category list)
training.regularisation: data augmentation: drop random non-violated categories; drop all violated categories and relabel safe; shuffle category indices

other.note: batch size 2 as printed; whether per device or global is not stated

inference.decoding: first-token probability of safe/unsafe read as classifier score; single-token generation for 1-vs-all
inference.samples: single evaluation per item; no seeds or repeats stated
inference.prompting: Llama Guard prompt with guidelines, classification type, conversation, output format. Zero-shot: category names and descriptions of target taxonomy. Few-shot: 2 to 4 examples per category, mix of unsafe and hard-negative safe.

metrics.name: AUPRC
metrics.definition: area under precision-recall curve on the unsafe class

metrics.name: Precision/Recall/F1
metrics.definition: threshold 0.5, for baselines without probabilities (Azure, GPT-4)

eval.protocol: Binary score for APIs = max over per-category scores (Eq 1). Per-category: 1-vs-all for Llama Guard (only category of interest in prompt); 1-vs-benign for baseline APIs off-policy (drops other-category positives, possibly optimistic). Azure integer 0-6 binarised with threshold 1-6 chosen for best average precision on the dataset. Llama Guard main results use adapted zero-shot (taxonomy and description, no examples). No seeds or significance tests.

limits: Common-sense knowledge limited by training and pretraining data; may give wrong judgements.
Fine-tuning data and most pretraining data are English; no guarantee for other languages.
No claim of perfect policy coverage; labels are from a single in-house red team.
May be susceptible to prompt injection attacks.
When prompted as a chat model it may generate unsafe language (no chat safety tuning).
Internal test set is in-domain (same taxonomy, same data process) so 0.945 is a ceiling; off-policy baselines use 1-vs-benign which may be optimistic.
AUPRC cannot be computed for Azure and GPT-4, so main comparison excludes them; GPT-4 and Azure compared at threshold 0.5 in the appendix only.
Training optimizer, schedule, seeds and exact prompt text (Figure 1 is an image) are not stated; no variance reported.
Dated: 2023 taxonomy of six categories and Llama2-7b backbone.

terms.definition: classifying the user messages (prompts) or the agent messages (responses) as two separate moderation tasks, drawn by change of wording in the instruction
one prediction task per category where only that category is positive and all other samples are negatives
like 1-vs-all but positives from other categories are dropped, leaving only benign negatives
